scenario: LSER.14.1 — a sliding window is the half-open (t−W, t], so a sample EXACTLY W old is outside it. One sample absorbed at t=0 into a `mean sliding 10_min`; the clock advances by exactly 600000000000 ns; an upsert of the same identity re-evaluates `where r.mean < 5.0` at assert. The only sample is exactly W old, so the window is empty, the read is cold ([LSER.19.8]) and `null < 5.0` does not fire ([LNUL.4.3]). A runtime keeping the closed [t−W, t] reads the mean 1.0 and fires. Path: libds `series_read_dispatch` → `series_window_emptied` (`>=`); Mercury `ds.series.in_window` (`Age < WindowNs`). The t=0 assert is cold (no instance yet) and must not fire either. Positive control: LSER.14.1_edge_sample_is_out_count_fires; the other side of the edge: LSER.14.1_inside_edge_sample_is_in_count_fires.
rules_ds:
use default

schema Reading scope logical:
    entity_id: String key
    v: Float mutable

schema Warm scope logical:
    d: Int key

series Reading.v:
    mean sliding 10_min

rule edge_mean:
    Reading r where r.mean < 5.0
->
    emit Warm logical d: 0
